title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
statement_short: Given the root of a complete binary tree, return the number of the nodes in the tree. Design an algorithm that runs in less than O(n) time complexity.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 5 \* 10^4, 0 <= Node.val <= 5 \* 10^4, tree is guaranteed to be complete
hint: Less than O(n) time mandate leverages complete tree properties to binary search existence of leaf nodes in O(log^2 n) time.
keywords: root of a complete binary tree
why_not: Right: Binary Search combined with tree height calculations tests leaf node existence in O(log^2 n) time, meeting the < O(n) constraint. Not Tree DFS: Standard recursive traversal visits every node in O(n) time, failing the required sub-linear time limit. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal queue visits all nodes in O(n) time and O(w) space. Not Math / Geometry: Formula 2^h - 1 calculates full tree node count, but leaf level gaps require binary search path checking.
complexity: O(log^2 n) time, O(log n) space
